Required courses: English I (9), English II (10), a junior English (CCV English Composition or American Literature), a senior English (VTSU English Gateway to Literature or Senior Seminar); United States History (required to graduate); Freshman Seminar (all freshmen); PE 9 (entry level for freshmen); Health I
Science progression for the 3 required credits: 9th Earth & Environmental Science; 10th Biology & Science Investigations; 11th/12th a Physical Science or Life Science course
graduation_requirements.raw_text: English: 4 credits Science: 3 credits Math: 3 credits Global Studies: 3 credits (1 US History) Fine Arts: 1 credit Health: .5 credit Physical Education: 1.5 credits Electives: 5.5 credits TOTAL: 21.5 Students will demonstrate proficiency in each area of the Proficiency Based Graduation Requirements (PBGRs). To demonstrate proficiency, students must attain an overall course score of 2.01 or higher. To meet graduation requirements, students demonstrate proficiency through a minimum of the above courses and/or by accessing equivalent learning through Flexible Pathways.

courses.description: English I is a co-taught course that is designed to introduce students to the rigors of high school English study. Through this course, students will study various literary genres to help develop cognitive skills and abilities to think, analyze, organize, and express their ideas clearly and effectively. Throughout the year we will explore the writing processes and academic literacy skills which will include interpretation, comprehension, analysis, and evaluation of literary and informational texts. Attention to grammar and conventions of standard written English are a “must” in this class. The class will comprise a variety of short stories, novels, and supportive non-fiction to help shed light on the importance of the literary experience.
courses.fulfills_text: English I (freshman requirement)

courses.description: English II is a sophomore English course. Students will take a tour around the globe, visiting various countries and cultures through the lens of literature, short stories, film, and essays. Students will continue their understanding of major literary techniques and genre, while practicing analysis, close-reading and interpretation. Students will also write in a variety of modes, honing their planning, revising and editing skills on essays and short timed-writes. Vocabulary and literary term development are woven into each unit.
courses.fulfills_text: English II (sophomore requirement)

courses.description: In this Dual Enrollment course, juniors develop effective composition skills and research techniques. Students learn strategies for organizing, evaluating, and revising their work through extensive reading of a variety of essay styles and literary texts; apply writing and research techniques to their papers; and demonstrate proficiency in first-year college-level writing and information literacy. This course will offer college credit through CCV.
courses.fulfills_text: Juniors are required to take one of the following
courses.notes: Listed in the dual enrollment list as CCV English Composition ENG 1061

courses.description: This course explores works from the canon of American literature and contemporary popular works of literature. Students will critically and analytically read short stories, novels and historic fiction. Students will write in a variety of forms in response to the text.
courses.fulfills_text: Juniors are required to take one of the following

courses.description: This Dual Enrollment course, open to seniors, introduces students to the study of literature, fiction, poetry and drama, as a university discipline. Students will develop their abilities to read perceptively and write effectively, using personal connections, formal strategies, and literary concepts to interpret and appreciate literature. Each semester the course will focus on a specific topic such as touchstone texts or popular literature. This course will offer college credit through VTSU.
courses.fulfills_text: Seniors are required to take one of the following
courses.notes: Listed in the dual enrollment list as VTSU English Gateway to Literature ENG 1101

courses.description: Senior Seminar is designed to help prospective graduates hone ELA skills for career and college readiness, equally. First semester students will demonstrate mastery of reading and writing skills through an exploration of literature that inspires the individual to understand who he or she is, and forge a meaningful path beyond high school. Second semester, students will complete their proficiencies, write a resume, practice an interview, conduct college level research, and write senior speeches.
courses.fulfills_text: Seniors are required to take one of the following

courses.description: In this dual enrollment public speaking class, we will work on becoming confident, prepared public speakers! Students will learn about rhetorical appeals through viewing and reading famous speeches. In addition, students will craft and deliver their own short speeches on a variety of topics. As this is a college class, students should be self-directed learners and willing to complete a higher-level workload.
courses.fulfills_text: Elective Courses (not used for the required 4 credits)
courses.notes: Listed in the dual enrollment list as CCV Effective Speaking ENG 1070

courses.description: This exciting English credit will explore both classical villains from literature such as Dr. Frankenstein in Shelley's Frankenstein, Nurse Ratched in One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest, The Ghost in Beloved, Claudius in Hamlet, and villains in contemporary fiction such as the shark in Jaws, Hannibal Lecter in Silence of the Lambs, Snow in The Hunger Games, Voldemort in Harry Potter, and many more! We will explore the role of the villain, and the construction of a villainous character. Likewise we will study the hero's journey, and their imperfect characters such as Odysseus in The Odyssey, Sherlock Holmes, Atticus Finch, and Frodo Baggins. The group will select our reading materials, as well as a collection of films!
courses.fulfills_text: Elective Courses (not used for the required 4 credits)

courses.description: Everyone loves a good murder mystery. It is the #1 most popular genre! We will study the construction of a murder mystery novel, identify what makes a good one, and dive into as many murder mysteries as we can, playing detective as we collect clues! Some great reads to be included: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder, The Woman in Cabin Ten, One of us is lying, The Dinner Party, We Were Liars, I must Betray You, and even some Hardy Boys and Nancy Drew! We will have to visit Sherlock Holmes, of course. Likewise, we will throw in the classic Agatha Christie works, and Alfred Hitchcock films! This is sure to be a fun way to tackle some good reads, and puzzle over some very interesting and complicated characters.
courses.fulfills_text: Elective Courses (not used for the required 4 credits)

courses.description: This course is a one year course that offers 0.5 English credit.Students will explore topics in society and history, and read literature in conjunction with those topics. It is a deep dive into social issues, using a variety of media such as film, fiction, essays, articles, art, music, and fiction.
courses.fulfills_text: Elective Courses (not used for the required 4 credits)
courses.notes: Description says "a one year course that offers 0.5 English credit"; length unclear

courses.description: Students in this course will acquire a foundation of knowledge to make decisions while driving that will ensure their safety and the safety of others on the roadway. The Driver Education Course is a decision-making process. Students will become familiar with Vermont motor vehicle laws, and learn to drive and manage their motor vehicle in various environments including city, rural and interstate driving. The course will cover the effects of drug use on the driver and the consequences of negative choices related to a driver’s personal health and safety. To satisfactorily complete the driver education course, and meet the State Requirements, a minimum score of 80 must be achieved on the road test and students are required to earn a minimum overall average of a 3.0 for Proficient in the classroom content. Students must also meet the minimum State Requirement of attendance at 30 hours of classroom sessions and 6 hours of guided behind the wheel instruction and 6 hours of observation instruction. In order for the student to satisfactorily complete the course, they must pass both the classroom and driving components. The intent of Driver Education is to help students develop knowledge, skills, attitudes and habits that can serve them for a lifetime of driving and enable them to become responsible drivers who are committed to embracing a low-risk driving style, skill and mindset.
courses.prerequisites: Sophomore standing, age of at least 15 and in possession of a Vermont Learner’s Permit. *Students must provide the School Registrar, Amy Klinger with their official Vermont Learner’s permit prior to registering/requesting this course*The paper receipt of testing is not adequate to enroll. You need to have access to a responsible, sober, licensed 25+ years aged driver who will drive with you throughout the course. It is highly recommended that you have a minimum of five hours of driving time before registering for the course.

courses.description: This class explores critical aspects of personal well-being and responsible decision-making. Students will delve into developing healthy habits and routines that promote physical, emotional, and mental wellness. The curriculum also addresses substance misuse prevention, fostering an understanding of mental health challenges, and strategies for seeking help. Additionally, the course covers sexual health and identity, emphasizing respectful and informed decision-making. Finally, students will learn about building positive relationships and effective communication skills to navigate social interactions and support networks. This comprehensive approach equips students with essential knowledge and skills to lead healthy and balanced lives.
courses.fulfills_text: 0.5 credit in Health

courses.description: Students will explore the concept of mental resilience and strategies for developing strong psychological fortitude. The curriculum will cover topics such as stress management, coping mechanisms, and building emotional intelligence. Students will learn practical techniques to enhance their ability to navigate challenges, setbacks, and pressure effectively. A key component of this course will involve studying individuals who have conquered adversity and demonstrated remarkable resilience. By examining the stories and experiences of resilient individuals, students will gain insight into the characteristics and behaviors that contribute to mental toughness. Through discussions, activities, and real life scenarios, students will have the opportunity to draw inspiration and learn from these role models. Additionally, the course will address the importance of mindset, self confidence, and positive thinking in fostering mental toughness. By the end of the course, students will be empowered with the tools to build and maintain mental toughness, enabling them to face adversity with confidence and resilience in their own lives.
courses.fulfills_text: 0.5 credit in Health

courses.course_name: Substance Abuse, Crime, and Public Health
courses.description: In this class, students will explore the complex interplay between substance abuse, criminal behavior, and public health outcomes. The course will cover the impact of substance misuse on individuals, families, and communities, including the correlation between substance abuse and crime rates. Students will examine public health strategies aimed at prevention, intervention, and treatment of substance use disorders. Additionally, the curriculum will address the legal and ethical dimensions surrounding substance abuse, including policies and interventions designed to mitigate its societal impact. Through discussions, case studies, and research projects, students will gain a deeper understanding of this critical intersection and develop insights into promoting healthier communities and reducing harm related to substance abuse and crime.
courses.fulfills_text: 0.5 credit in Health

courses.description: An innovative course empowering high school students to address and rectify health-related issues within our school community. This comprehensive program combines the power of data-driven insights, collaboration with school administration, and the creative problem-solving approach of design thinking to foster holistic well-being and create a healthier, more supportive, and thriving school environment. Our mission is to cultivate a cohort of informed and passionate health advocates who actively contribute to creating positive change. Through a blend of data analysis and design thinking, students will develop the skills needed to address health challenges creatively, collaboratively, and effectively.
courses.fulfills_text: 0.5 credit in Elective

courses.description: First-year physical education will delve into various games and activities, encompassing net games, invasion games, striking and fielding games, and target games. Our approach will prioritize skill development, strategic thinking, and team collaboration through focused activities. Alongside games, the curriculum will cover the safe and efficient utilization of the fitness center, with a focus on identifying muscles and engaging in targeted exercises to enhance both strength and flexibility. Moreover, it will foster healthy habits related to fitness, impacting overall health positively.
courses.notes: Heading: "PE 9 - Entry Level course for all Freshman"

courses.description: Students will delve into a range of net games such as Volleyball, Badminton, Pickleball, Nitroball, and numerous other variants. Throughout the semester, we'll focus on different aspects of each game, honing skills, strategy, and teamwork. Additionally, students will gain insights into officiating games and organizing various types of tournaments.

Science and modern technology has provided deeper insight into how our minds and bodies change based on our focus, intentions, environment, habits, stress and behaviors. With a scientific approach we will investigate these new perspectives and experience transformative mindful practices to explore our thoughts, beliefs, emotions and paradigms to create sustainable shifts towards optimal health, wellness and living. Students will gain a better understanding of how their nutritional choices contribute positively and negatively towards their health, both physically and mentally. The ultimate goal of the course is for students to come away with an understanding of how to maintain a healthy mind and body for the rest of their lives.
courses.fulfills_text: .5 credit & .5 Science credit
courses.notes: *Sophomores may be eligible based on instructor approval! Also listed under Science electives (page 34) as 0.5 Science Credit & 0.5 PE Credit; offered 2026/27.

courses.description: This course is designed to give students the opportunity to learn fitness concepts and conditioning techniques used for obtaining optimal physical fitness. Students will benefit from comprehensive resistance training and cardiorespiratory endurance activities. Students will learn the basic fundamentals of strength training, aerobic training, and overall fitness training and conditioning. The course includes lecture and activity sessions both indoors and outdoors. Students will be empowered to make health enhancing choices, meet challenges, and develop positive behaviors in fitness, wellness, and movement activity for a lifetime.

This course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of healthy living and a well-balanced lifestyle. Through a combination of theoretical and practical approaches, students will learn the significance of nutrition, culinary creativity, fitness development, and lifetime activities. Students will explore a range of topics, including the benefits of a healthy diet, the relationship between physical activity and health, and various methods to maintain a balanced lifestyle. With hands-on activities, students will learn practical culinary skills and techniques,and how to prepare healthy and delicious meals. Additionally, the course offers a wide variety of fitness activities, such as strength training, cardiovascular exercise, and endurance training, among others. The class encourages a lifetime approach to health and wellness, aiming to promote good habits that students can carry into their adult lives.

This Physical Education course focuses on leadership, mentoring, and teaching through physical activity. High school students will design and lead engaging games and activities for middle school students during lunch or recess periods. Throughout the course, students will gain hands-on experience in planning, organizing, and facilitating group activities while developing communication, coaching, and leadership skills. This course is ideal for students interested in working with youth, pursuing coaching, or taking on leadership roles in camp or recreation settings.

This course serves as a stepping stone into Algebra. Designed to establish a foundation, it delves into essential mathematical concepts crucial for success in higher-level algebraic studies. The curriculum topics include, including algebraic expressions, integers, equations, decimals, fractions, exponents, ratios, proportions, percents, area, and graphing. Through comprehensive exploration, this course equips students with the necessary skills and knowledge to confidently transition into the study of Algebra and beyond.

This course is recommended for all students. Algebra 1 course topics include solving linear, absolute value and exponential equations and inequalities, solving systems of equations using a variety of methods, an introduction to the study of functions and function notation, graphing and interpreting linear, absolute value, quadratic and exponential functions, and using these functions to model real world applications.
courses.prerequisites: successful completion of Common Core Math 8

courses.description: This course is recommended for all students. Geometry course topics include; angles and angle pair relationships; parallel lines and transversals; perimeter and area of polygons and circles; similar and congruent triangles; the Pythagorean Theorem and right triangle trigonometry; and other properties and theorems related to circles, quadrilaterals, and other polygons.

This course is recommended for all students. Algebra 2 includes the study of right triangle trigonometry, quadratic and higher degree polynomial functions, and exponential and radical functions. Each family of functions is used to model data and the students practice writing, factoring, solving, evaluating, graphing and transforming the functions.

This course is recommended for students who plan to major in mathematics or science related fields. Topics in the course include complex numbers, rational and discontinuous functions, asymptotes and basic limits, analytic geometry, logarithmic and exponential functions, operations on functions, periodic functions, trigonometric identities, and probability.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Algebra 2 or recommendation of teacher

courses.description: AP Calculus AB is an advanced mathematics course that explores the fundamental concepts of change, limits, and the analysis of functions. Students will develop a deep understanding of rates of change using derivatives and learn to apply definite integrals to model net change in various real-world contexts. Through the study of limits, students will transition from discrete models to continuous functions, gaining insight into key calculus principles such as continuity, differentiation, and integration. The course emphasizes the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, highlighting the essential relationship between differentiation and integration. By analyzing the behaviors of functions, students will connect calculus concepts to solve problems across multiple disciplines, preparing them for further studies in mathematics, science, and engineering.

The purpose of this course is to gain an understanding of statistical principles. You will learn how to collect data (including simple sampling and experimental designs), summarize data using graphical and numerical techniques, examine data for patterns and relationships, and analyze data so you can draw valid and appropriate conclusions. You will also interpret and judge statistical information, including information embedded in computer output. You will focus on effectively presenting statistical information to general audiences. This class is offered with a dual enrollment option through the Vermont State University system. Full year course - alternating with Personal Finance.
courses.offering_note: Full year course - alternating with Personal Finance
courses.notes: Dual enrollment option through the Vermont State University system

courses.description: When will you use this math? Everyday for the rest of your life! How much money do you hope to make? What can you realistically expect your lifestyle to be like? Have you planned for your retirement? This course will explore how the decisions you make will affect your financial security and status. You will create a model for your life which will include choosing a career, making sure you are qualified, meeting your living expenses, taking on debt and paying it off over time, and saving in order to retire with enough wealth to sustain you in your senior years. After successfully completing this course students will be better equipped to make the important choices and avoid common pitfalls involved in living in our modern economy.

Math Lab is a supportive, hands-on course designed to strengthen students’ understanding of core mathematical concepts through interactive exploration and personalized instruction. This course is ideal for students who need additional time and strategies to grasp foundational math skills or want to deepen their problem-solving abilities. In Math Lab, students will: ● Reinforce topics from their regular math classes (Algebra, Geometry, etc.) ● Engage in guided practice, collaborative problem-solving, and real-world math applications ● Receive targeted support based on individual learning needs ● Use technology, manipulatives, and visual models to explore concepts in depth ● Develop confidence and independence in mathematical thinking

Teacher Approval is required. 7:30 a.m. on B-Days. Let’s jam! The High School Stage Band explores a diverse range of musical styles, adapting its repertoire to the strengths of the ensemble. Students will develop improvisation skills, stylistic accuracy, and ensemble techniques while learning how to lead productive and collaborative rehearsals. This course provides intermediate musicians with a strong foundation for performing, arranging, and even creating their own music. This course is open to experienced instrumentalists and vocalists. Prior approval is required. Membership is determined by an audition or a meeting with the director to discuss placement. Selection is based on the following: 1. Vocal and/or instrumental ability. 2. Previous musical experience. 3. Commitment to rehearsals and performances. 4. Blend and balance of the ensemble Students should be ready to engage, experiment, practice, and contribute to the ensemble. Performances are an essential part of the course, providing students with real-world playing experience. Students could have the opportunity to audition and participate in district music festivals. To maintain a strong foundation in musicianship, Stage Band vocalists must also be enrolled in HS Chorus, and Stage Band instrumentalists must be enrolled in HS Instrumental Studies: Modern Band. Performances are a required component of the course, including the Winter Concert (mid-term), Spring Performances (final exam), and Graduation (June). Membership status will be reviewed at the end of each semester. If you are ready to collaborate, perform, and grow as a musician, Stage Band is the place for you!
courses.notes: (Full Year Course); teacher approval required (audition); 7:30 a.m. on B-Days

courses.description: Love to sing? Join the HS Chorus and make music with friends! No experience is necessary—just bring your enthusiasm. The more, the merrier! In this full-year course, students will collaborate to shape their musical experience, with song selections influenced by ensemble members. The chorus has the potential to develop into a soprano-alto-tenor-bass (SATB) performing ensemble, exploring a wide variety of musical styles. Along the way, students will strengthen their vocal technique, musicianship, and ensemble skills in a fun and supportive environment—with no pressure to sing solo! Students will also have the opportunity to audition for district music festivals. Performances are a required part of the course, including the Winter Concert (mid-term), Spring Performances (final exam), and Graduation (June). Membership status will be reviewed at the end of each semester. Come sing, collaborate, and grow as a musician—HS Chorus is waiting for you!
courses.notes: (Full Year Course); heading lists Grades 8 - 12

courses.description: Looking to have fun while learning an instrument and sharpening your musical skills? This course is open to students in grades 9-12. This is for students with or without musical experience. The instrumental instruction meets you where you are, helping you practice, rehearse, and grow at your own pace. Whether you want to refine your technique, expand your repertoire, or simply enjoy making music, Concert Band is the perfect opportunity to learn and grow! Students will develop their performance skills, instrumental technique, and music theory knowledge while gaining valuable experience playing collaboratively, deepening your understanding of your instrument, and building confidence as a musician. Join us and make music a part of your journey!
courses.notes: (Full Year Course)

courses.description: Earth & Environmental Science focuses on scientific exploration of the atmosphere, hydrosphere, and lithosphere. Through the course, students will critically examine topics related to meteorology, climate, energy, geology, glaciology, hydrology, and astronomy. Students will engage in the skills of being a scientist through a hands-on, project-based learning model.
courses.fulfills_text: Progression for obtaining the 3 required Science credits: 9th grade: Earth & Environmental Science
courses.notes: Heading "Earth Science"; description titled Earth & Environmental Science

courses.description: Biology and Science Investigations is a survey of classic Biology concepts: the chemistry of life, cell biology processes, heredity, ecology, and evolution. The second semester of the course includes the completion of a substantial science investigation project on a topic of each student’s choosing: they design and conduct a controlled experiment or research study, and communicate their results in an oral presentation to a panel of judges at the NHS Science Fair. This course will allow students to practice and develop the skills of a scientist, and experience a variety of hands-on and project-based learning opportunities.
courses.fulfills_text: Progression for obtaining the 3 required Science credits: 10th grade: Biology & Science Investigations

courses.description: General Chemistry is an inquiry-based course that examines matter and the changes it undergoes. Experiments and activities are used to introduce concepts including the structure of atoms and chemical compounds, the relationships among the elements on the periodic table, chemical and physical transformations, and the measurement and calculations of chemical quantities. Students will make connections between Chemistry concepts and the world around them, exploring real-world applications of the topics they explore throughout the course. Students who complete this course will develop an understanding of interconnections among the sciences, technology, society, and the environment. This course will prepare students for a college-level Chemistry lab course.
courses.prerequisites: 2 years of high school science AND 2 years of math
courses.fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course
courses.offering_note: Offered as needed; Physical Science options offered on a rotating basis

courses.description: This course is intended to extend student understanding of atomic structure, chemical formulae and reactions including chemical bonding, mole ratios, stoichiometry, and heats of reaction. Chemistry laboratory experiments are regularly completed to help support the students’ understanding of these concepts. In addition, real world applications of chemistry concepts will be emphasized. This course will move at a fast pace and involve an in-depth exploration of Chemistry concepts, and such, students will be expected to meet a high standard of engagement in this course, both in and outside of the scheduled class period. This course will meet college requirements for a Chemistry lab course. This course is a dual-enrollment course, where students can receive 4 college credits upon successful completion of the course (per the partner college Science department expectations).
courses.prerequisites: 2 years of high school science AND concurrent enrollment in Algebra 2 or higher
courses.fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course
courses.notes: Dual-enrollment; students can receive 4 college credits

courses.description: Forensic science is an inquiry, skill and content-based course that studies the connection between science and law. This course asks students to look at what the evidence tells them about a crime, suspect and/or crime scene. Students will learn to examine evidence as they extend their biological, physical and chemical knowledge from their previous years of science experience. Students can expect a mix of hands-on learning opportunities, case studies, documentaries, and written components.
courses.prerequisites: Two years of high school science
courses.fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course
courses.notes: Heading has "**" (unexplained). Not offered 2026-27.

courses.description: This course covers general physics concepts including motion, energy, and matter. Aspects of sustainability, climate, astronomy, and engineering will be woven throughout the units. This course will foster curiosity and support hands-on learning, collaborative projects, creative expression, 21st century technology skills, and connecting science to the real world. In previous years, students have participated in design challenges like the VTC Bridge Building Competition. This course will prepare students for a college-level Physics lab course, and students who are interested in pursuing engineering or math majors should plan to take this course.
courses.prerequisites: 2 years of high school science AND concurrent enrollment in Algebra 2 or higher
courses.fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course
courses.notes: Heading has "**" (unexplained)

courses.description: Anatomy introduces and explores the structure and function of the human body and focuses on how the body systems relate to one another in organization, adaptation, and homeostasis. Students will explore careers in the human biology field and make personal connections to the content. This course will involve discussion, laboratory activities, projects, and dissections, and will source textbook material, models, and clinical studies as resources for gaining knowledge and experience with the concepts. Students who are interested in pursuing medical or veterinary careers are encouraged to take this course.
courses.fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course

courses.description: This college-level course is an introduction to the study of life, including cells, organisms, ecosystems, and evolution, and the skills of a biologist. We will take a deeper dive into topics introduced in 10th grade Biology, and explore additional topics and real world applications of biology concepts. This course will include lecture and laboratory components, and will move at a fast pace with in-depth exploration of topics; as such, students will be expected to meet a high standard of engagement in this course, both in and outside of the scheduled class period. This is a dual-enrollment course and students can receive 4 college credits towards a Biology Lab course upon successful completion of the course (per VTSU Science department expectations).
courses.prerequisites: Biology AND and 2 years of high school math
courses.fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course
courses.offering_note: Offered as needed in place of VTSU EnvSci; dual enrollment courses offered on a rotating basis
courses.notes: Students can receive 4 college credits towards a Biology Lab course

courses.description: This course explores the environment and solutions to environmental problems. Students will explore fundamental concepts in physical and ecological processes that shape our environment, and the role human civilizations have in shaping the environment. Emphasis is placed on examining solutions to current environmental problems including aspects of soil, water, and air pollution, ecosystem services, biomimicry, environmental toxicology, and more. Central to this course are hands-on labs, field studies, and student-designed projects. This is a dual-enrollment course and students can receive 4 college credits upon successful completion of the course (per VTSU Science department expectations).
courses.fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course
courses.notes: Not offered 2026-27; students can receive 4 college credits

courses.description: This semester class is an opportunity for students to explore the science of their everyday lives and the world around us. The course will integrate natural and physical sciences through topics like consumer chemistry, biomimicry, science in history, citizen science, climate & sustainability, and more. Students will build their investigative, lab, and communication skills as they engage in hands-on and project-based learning, through both collaborative and independent learning opportunities. If you are naturally curious about the everyday world around you, this class will allow you the opportunity to discover some of the science behind your wonders.
courses.notes: Science Electives - Offered beyond the suggested progression of courses

courses.description: This course is intended to equip students with a good understanding and appreciation of U.S. History from the Civil War to the present. Key themes include: domestic politics and policies; foreign policy and America’s changing role in the world; race and minority issues; our changing Constitution; and the interaction of citizens and government. Building students’ critical reading and content area writing skills will also be emphasized.
courses.fulfills_text: Required to Graduate

courses.description: This course will cover world history from prehistory to the present. Units include the Neolithic Period, Ancient World, Medieval Period, the Renaissance, the Enlightenment, the Age of Revolutions, the Industrial Revolution, the Age of Imperialism, the World Wars and the Holocaust, the Cold War, and Globalization. Major historical figures like Gandhi, Mao, and Luther will be spotlighted, as well as key events and inventions that reshaped the world. Changing systems of government, economics and political philosophies will also be examined. This hands-on learning class will emphasize critical reading and thinking skills, essay writing, and classroom discussion.

This seminar course is geared towards mastering the basics of college level World History and preparing students to pass the AP World History exam in the spring for college credit. Students should expect to do independent reading and writing at the college level and engage in class discussions to heighten understanding. The course surveys major themes in world history from 1200 C.E. through the present.
courses.notes: **Teacher permission encouraged

courses.description: Welcome to the exciting world of Government, Politics, and Economics. Yes, I did say exciting. Why, you might ask? It is because everything you and I think of as important and interesting in your life (sports, music, fashion, cute girls/boys, hanging with your bro’s) can all be connected to something in Government, Politics, and Economics. But that’s not all. Oh, no that is not all. It also includes such big concepts as warfare, values, law, punishment, independence, among many others. Over the course of the year we will study complex ideas like: what is the best form of government, what is the social contract, what are the rights and responsibilities of a citizen, what is wealth, how should we spend it, and some more direct applications: what do the democratic and republican party stand for, what does a town manager do, should a city build a stadium for a sports team, and many, many more. Hold on to your hats, you will be ready to step out of this course and become the active, informed citizen that our founders envisioned.

The Advanced Placement program in United States History is designed to provide students with the analytical skills and factual knowledge necessary to pass the Advanced Placement exam for college credit. Students will learn to access primary source materials - their relevance to a given interpretive problem, their reliability, and their importance - and to weigh the evidence and interpretations presented in historical scholarship. The course covers pre-European settlement and exploration of the New World to the present. The course culminates with the Advanced Placement Examination in United States History in the spring. This course is designed to complement the AP Literature syllabus.
courses.notes: **Teacher permission recommended

courses.description: Humans are storytellers. From our earliest ancestors we have filled our history with different myths and stories to give meaning to our lives. Over the past 150 years we took these stories that were told through verbal and written mediums and changed this to a visual one. This essential course follows the development of the medium of the moving image. We will explore the development of movies from short, silent oddities to the blockbusters of the modern day. Students will watch critically how movies have changed to both reflect and shape the world around them. With the skills and knowledge of the medium of film that you develop will change how you watch them. If you like movies you’ll never watch them quite the same way again.

For those students who enjoyed Film Studies I or who are more interested in the creative process behind making a film. In this exciting course we will not only continue our study of great films we’ll focus on the actual process. Ranging from screenplays, filming and editing students will adopt some of the techniques we examine through study and film to create their own movie.

This course will introduce students to the basic tenets of psychology. This course grapples with such complex issues as the nature of mankind, the impact of our subconscious, human development, psychological disorders and their treatments. Designed as an introductory survey course, we will take a world-wide run through the basics of psychology with emphasis on the major theories and theorists of psychology, how our psychological profile changes over our lifespan, the link between our body and brains, the process of learning, social psychology, psychological disorders, their diagnosis and treatment and the major motivators in life.

Introduction to sociology is a riveting course that is a perfect complement to psychology. Sociology focuses on the interplay of people in group settings. The course will study the development of the field, including some of the leading theorists. Key units focus on social inequality: including race, gender, and class, social institutions: including family, education, and government and how they function and the dynamics of social change.

World Religions is designed to provide students with an introduction to the diverse and complex religious traditions that exist across the globe. Throughout the semester, students will explore various religious beliefs, practices, and rituals of major world religions such as Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Judaism. The course aims to foster a greater understanding and appreciation of the role of religion in shaping cultures, societies, and individuals. Additionally, students will examine the historical and social contexts that have influenced the development of religions, as well as current issues and challenges faced by religious communities around the world. By the end of the course, students will have gained a deeper understanding of the diversity and complexity of religious traditions, and will be better equipped to engage with and respect individuals from different religious backgrounds.

In this dynamic class on current events, students will engage with the ever-evolving landscape of global affairs, exploring the latest developments, controversies, and trends shaping our world. Through lively discussions, critical analysis of news articles, and multimedia presentations, participants will deepen their understanding of pressing issues spanning politics, economics, culture, and technology. From geopolitical tensions to social movements, from breakthrough scientific discoveries to emerging challenges, this course offers a comprehensive and insightful examination of the contemporary world, empowering students to become informed and active global citizens.

Civics class will introduce students to the foundations of government, citizenship, and civic responsibility. Students explore how local, state, and federal governments function, examine the rights and responsibilities of citizens, and analyze current events and public policy. Through discussion, debate, and real-world connections, the course encourages students to think critically, engage respectfully with different perspectives, and become informed, active participants in their communities.

Cartography & Culture is an engaging high school course that explores the powerful relationship between maps and the people who create and use them. Students learn the fundamentals of map-making while examining how geography, history, and cultural perspectives shape the way places are represented. Through hands-on projects and analysis of maps from around the world, students develop skills in spatial thinking, data interpretation, and critical analysis. The course encourages students to question bias in mapping, understand diverse worldviews, and create their own maps that tell meaningful stories about communities and cultures.
courses.notes: Appears at the top of the Visual Arts page (page 38) but follows the Social Studies listings

courses.description: This introductory course provides students with a comprehensive foundation in visual art through hands-on exploration of multiple media, including drawing, painting, printmaking, photography, and introductory three-dimensional work. Students will develop technical skills while strengthening their understanding of the Elements of Art and Principles of Design. Emphasis is placed on observation, composition, color theory, creative problem-solving, and experimentation with materials and processes. Through studio projects, critique, and reflection, students will build confidence in their artistic abilities while developing both technical proficiency and thoughtful visual expression.

Advanced Studio is a choice-based course designed for students who wish to deepen their artistic practice and explore more independent, self-directed work. Students will develop projects using a variety of media, which may include experimental painting, printmaking, book arts, photography, sculpture, mixed media, and installation. Emphasis is placed on concept development, material exploration, and intentional artistic decision-making. Through project proposals, critique, and reflection, students will strengthen their technical skills, refine their personal voice, and learn to communicate ideas through visual form.
courses.prerequisites: Foundations of Visual Art (or teacher recommendation)

courses.description: This introductory course explores the fundamentals of ceramics, focusing on the techniques used to create three-dimensional forms. Students will develop skills in the three core hand-building methods: pinching, coil construction, and slab construction. Through the creation of both functional and sculptural pieces, students will learn to shape, refine, and decorate their work using various surface treatments and glazing techniques. Emphasis will be placed on craftsmanship, creativity, and personal expression as students gain confidence in working with clay and develop their own artistic approach to ceramic design.

This advanced ceramics course builds upon the foundational skills learned in Ceramics I, challenging students to refine their craftsmanship and deepen their artistic problem-solving abilities. Students will further develop their proficiency in pinching, coil construction, and slab construction, pushing these techniques to create more complex and sophisticated forms. In addition, Ceramics II introduces wheel throwing while allowing students to explore new approaches to ceramic design. Emphasis will also be placed on surface treatment, glazing techniques, and a deeper understanding of kiln firing and loading. Through hands-on practice and creative exploration, students will expand their technical skills, artistic expression, and knowledge of ceramic processes.

This course encourages students to move beyond traditional painting by combining drawing, painting, printmaking, collage, and textural processes to create layered and expressive artwork. Students will experiment with acrylic paint, mixed-media materials, unconventional tools, and surface treatments while exploring abstraction, personal symbolism, and contemporary approaches to image-making. Emphasis is placed on creative risk-taking, material experimentation, and developing a personal visual language through process-driven work.

Russian Exploratory is for students who would like to learn some Russian and have fun with language learning that is very different. Students will learn the Cyrillic alphabet, lots of fun vocabulary and also learn about Russia as a nation. We will also watch the series Chernobyl to learn about the explosion of the nuclear power plant in Chernobyl. And we will learn two songs!
courses.notes: Semester One; Elective

courses.description: Spanish Conversation is for students who need a slower pace in the study of language. Students will benefit from more time to study grammar, acquire vocabulary, practice pronunciation and will receive more in-class support on assessments such as projects and memorizations. Students will use Duolingo to guide their program of study. They will also use sites including: Gimkit, Blooket, Wordwall, and Quizlet. This class is for students who want to learn some Spanish and earn a language credit but will not take a second year of language.
courses.notes: Semester Two; Elective

courses.description: The emphasis in Spanish I is on building a vocabulary and learning everyday Spanish. Reading, writing, speaking and listening skills are all stressed in order to build a basic level of proficiency. Students will create a variety of oral and written texts to express their understanding. By the end of this level, students will be able to describe and converse about themselves, their family, their school day and their hobbies.

At the intermediate level, emphasis will be placed on improving the students’ ability to understand spoken Spanish as well as to speak the language more fluidly. Students will create cultural presentations, participate in conversations about current events, and recite songs and poetry. By the end of this level, students should be comfortable carrying on daily conversations regarding topics such as food, shopping, travel and health/medical needs.

This course continues the fundamentals of the Spanish language skills covering grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation. Vocabulary units go into depth regarding the ways students spend their time, family dynamics, and daily routines. The course includes conversation, reading and writing exercises and provides an introduction to the arts and cultures of Spain, Latin America and Spanish-speaking peoples.
courses.prerequisites: Spanish II completion w/ 3.0 and teacher recommendation
courses.notes: Listed in the dual enrollment list as CCV Spanish I SPA 1011

courses.description: In Spanish level 4, students now have the skills to conduct a large percent of the class in the target language. Vocabulary units will focus around food, medical needs, and the environment. Students will do hands-on projects in each unit. The English part of class will focus on verb conjugation in the past and future tenses. By the end of four years, students should be proficient meaning they would be able to communicate in most basic situations of daily life.
courses.prerequisites: Spanish III completion w/ 3.0 and teacher recommendation
courses.notes: This course is a concurrent/dual enrollment college class conducted on our campus, led by Ms. McBride. Listed in the dual enrollment list as CCV Spanish II SPA 1012

courses.description: Pathways is a system that facilitates flexible and challenging individual and personal learning plans designed to recognize and nurture unique learning styles, interests, and strengths of individual students, and supports multiple pathways towards achievement and assessment of proficiencies. Individual paths for students can include, but are not limited to: experiential, service, blended, independent, online, skill-based, work-readiness, advanced college-readiness, and traditional learning. You will meet with your advisor and the Coordinator of Student Support in your school to discuss these options.
courses.notes: program; *see the Pathways section of this guide for more information*

courses.description: This course focuses on the fundamental disciplines of woodworking; that is, the proper execution of the basic skills and attention to detail leading to the development of self-confidence. Projects are designed to reinforce previously learned fundamentals. There is a heavy emphasis on hand tools although competency with power tools is also developed. Students choose projects of progressive complexity and utility; including carving of lettering, sculpture and small furniture making.

All freshmen will take this team-taught multidisciplinary course. This supportive course is designed to help support our freshmen as they transition to high school. Teachers will focus on organization, projects, executive functioning, team building, reading, writing, math, and myriad other skills. The team of teachers who run this course have designed it as a “bridge” between middle & high school expectations.
courses.notes: All freshmen will take this course

courses.description: This course will cover the important issues that you will encounter during your high school years; and help to prepare you for life beyond high school. We will investigate life management skills in the areas of personal, family, and community living; wellness, nutrition, and foods; consumer management (budgeting), living environments and job readiness. Students can take this class more than once with teacher permission.

AP Computer Science Principles is an introductory college-level computing course that introduces students to the breadth of the field of computer science. Students learn to design and evaluate solutions and to apply computer science to solve problems through the development of algorithms and programs. They incorporate abstraction into programs and use data to discover new knowledge. Students also explain how computing innovations and computing systems—including the internet—work, explore their potential impacts, and contribute to a computing culture that is collaborative and ethical.
courses.notes: Description titled AP Computer Science Principles

courses.description: This course is designed to equip middle/high school athletes with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue collegiate sports opportunities successfully. Students will explore key aspects of athletic preparation, including coaching principles, strength and conditioning tailored for their sport, and game film analysis to enhance performance. They will also develop athlete profiles, learn proper sports nutrition, and practice interview techniques to effectively present themselves to recruiters. Additionally, the course emphasizes sportsmanship, leadership, and the mental aspects of competition, ensuring students are well-rounded and prepared for the next level of their athletic journey.

The purpose of a Work-Based Learning is to provide an opportunity for juniors and seniors to gain on the job experience in a specific field of interest. Students connect classroom experiences to community and career experiences to prepare them for the future. We are hoping to offer this option in the future.
courses.notes: program; "We are hoping to offer this option in the future."

program; Internships Overview: can be taken for one semester or full year; students can earn Habits of Success; grades 11 and 12; approval from the school counselor necessary; employer or supervisor verification required; a contract outlining duties and skills must be completed. See your Coordinator of Work-Based Learning.

courses.description: Students may earn graduation PIs/credit via online courses. Our two current vendors are Vermont Virtual Learning Cooperative (VTVLC) and Brigham Young University (BYU). VTVLC is a partnership of Vermont schools that offer online courses that may not otherwise be available at NMHS or WMHS. The school assumes the cost of these courses. Prior approval from the Coordinator of Student Support is required. The course/grade will be recorded on the student’s transcript.
courses.notes: program; *Prior approval from the School Counselor & Principal is required

courses.course_name: CCV’s Introduction to College and Careers
courses.description: Introduction to College and Careers is a free 13-week course that provides students with the opportunity to explore the college experience within the context of their future career goals. For more information and a schedule of courses at all 12 CCV locations, please visit: www.gotocollegevt.org
courses.notes: program; free 13-week course

courses.description: Habits of Success are earned based on the student’s ability to demonstrate how they achieved them through their individual experience. HOS are approved by the supervisor and school counselor. Students will engage in direct personal service under an approved plan developed by the student and authorized by the school counselor. Service Learning builds character, empathy, commitment and engagement, all key qualities of both Northfield High School and of caring citizens. Students are responsible for keeping a weekly log documenting hours worked. Possibilities include: tutoring other students, helping senior citizens, improving the school or larger community.
courses.notes: program

courses.description: Students in grades 9-12 who have missed earning the proficient level for any Performance Indicator with a score between (1.8 - 2.0) may enroll in credit recovery to attempt to demonstrate those PI's at the proficient level. The student must meet with their teacher, advisor and obtain approval by a certified teacher from the content area of the respective Performance Indicator.
courses.notes: program

courses.department: Dual Enrollment / High School Completion Program
courses.description: Once in a while, students need a highly individualized plan to meet their graduation requirements - our alternative programming offers just that. In partnership with students and their families, NMHS will develop a schedule that supports personal and scholastic goals in an alternative setting and incorporates elements of community and work-based learning, social-emotional well-being, and academic requirements. This opportunity is only available to students aged 16 and older who have been recommended by the administrative team. For more information, please reach out to Michelle Aftuck, Christine High, or Lee Ann Monroe at 485-4500.
courses.notes: program; alternative programming; only available to students aged 16 and older recommended by the administrative team

courses.description: With the 2013 passage of the Flexible Pathways bill (S.130/Act77), students in the state of Vermont have the opportunity to take up to two college courses at participating Vermont state colleges/universities. Eligible students can use two Dual Enrollment vouchers during their 11th and/or 12th grade years. These vouchers can be used to take a college course at schools such as Norwich University, Community College of Vermont, Vermont Technical College, University of Vermont and more. Effective November 30, 2015, any student wanting to participate in a dual enrollment course must have this goal included in their Personalized Learning Plan (PLP). 11th and 12th grade students may enroll in college courses provided a schedule can be arranged to coordinate with the high school program. Your college course and grade will be recorded on your high school transcript.
courses.notes: program; *Prior approval from the Coordinator of Student Support is required. On-campus VSU/CCV courses are listed separately.

courses.description: Vermont students with senior standing have the opportunity to spend their entire last year of high school on a Vermont State College campus as a “freshman” college student through the Vermont Early College Program. Participating colleges are: Castleton University, Community College of Vermont, Goddard College, Northern Vermont University (Johnson & Lyndon campuses), Norwich University & VTC. Eligible students must be in excellent academic standing and successfully pass all placement tests required by the college. Students are financially liable for transportation, books and other college fees. See your Coordinator of Student Support for more information on the Early College Program and visit https://education.vermont.gov/student-learning/flexible-pathways/early-college
courses.notes: program; *Prior approval from the Coordinator of Student Support is required
